canonical_data: a workspace directory of Markdown identity/memory files (SOUL.md, IDENTITY.md, MEMORY.md), a SQLite database for tasks (FTS5), plans, and the memU semantic memory index, all on the operator's own host
strengths: Plans require explicit human approval before an implementation session spawns, and destructive tool calls require explicit consent, with a full audit trail of mutations
Runs as a single Python process (FastAPI + uvicorn + asyncio, no Docker or message queue required) light enough for a Raspberry Pi, and works off a Claude subscription with no API key
Dual-layer memory (curated hot Markdown memory plus a semantic SQLite index) and self-proposed, self-revised Markdown skills give the agent durable, inspectable state across restarts
weaknesses: Single-provider by design: the agent engine is built entirely on the Claude Agent SDK, so the runtime's behavior is coupled to Anthropic model access
Very early-stage adoption (80 stars, one primary maintainer) with no independent track record beyond its own README and test suite
Untrusted third-party content (Gmail, GitHub, Telegram) is only mitigated by a documented prompt-injection warning prefix, not sandboxed execution of ingested content
why_it_matters: A working, self-hosted example of a persistent agent runtime with real plan/approve governance and dual-layer memory built directly on a provider's own agent SDK rather than a bespoke orchestration layer.
